description: Five engineering students from Costa Rica who love technology, health, and innovation. Our team mixes Informatics, Biomedical, and Mechatronics Engineering, so we cover software, hardware, and health tech. Monsserratt is the Informatics Engineering student president at ULACIT, Pilar is the Biomedical Engineering student president there too, and Andy is a member of Startup Supernovas, ULACIT’s entrepreneurship club. We’re motivated, we listen to each other, and we like building things that matter
summary:
SilverPulse is a web-based prototype designed to support astronaut health monitoring before, during, and after space missions. It addresses the challenge of transforming fragmented physiological measurements into understandable information, especially when communication with Earth is delayed or interrupted.

The platform organizes physiological data, including heart rate, sleep, and physical activity, compares measurements with individual baselines, and generates explainable reports for medical review.

SilverPulse also simulates communication interruptions between a spacecraft and Earth. Medical reports are stored locally when the connection is unavailable and transmitted when communication resumes, allowing Earth-based personnel to review information and send feedback to the crew.

Built with React, FastAPI, and SQLite, our prototype demonstrates an integrated monitoring and communication workflow using clearly identified synthetic scenarios and sample public physiological data.

SilverPulse is an experimental decision-support prototype, not a clinically validated diagnostic system. Its goal is to improve continuity, transparency, and accessibility of health information during long-duration space missions.
details:
What is SilverPulse?

SilverPulse is a prototype health-monitoring and medical communication platform designed for long-duration space missions.

The project addresses two interconnected challenges: interpreting physiological data in an understandable way and maintaining continuity of medical information when communication with Earth becomes unavailable.

How does it work?

The platform imports physiological measurements, validates their sources, and compares them against personal baseline data. Its ORBIT VERIFY analysis system identifies relevant trends and generates structured, explainable reports.

A simulated communication system allows the spacecraft to store reports during a connection outage and transmit them when communication resumes. Medical personnel on Earth can review the information and send observations back to the spacecraft.

Our prototype demonstrates this complete process using synthetic astronaut scenarios.

Technologies

  • React, TypeScript and Vite for the user interface.
  • Python and FastAPI for the backend.
  • SQLite for data storage.
  • Automated testing with pytest, Vitest and Playwright.

Scientific foundation

NASA's Human Research Program provided scientific context about cardiovascular adaptation, sleep disturbances, reduced physical fitness and other health risks associated with spaceflight.

NASA's Delay/Disruption Tolerant Networking documentation informed the design of our application-level store-and-forward communication simulator.

We also incorporated a small sample from the public PhysioNet BIDMC physiological dataset for additional data-processing tests.

Innovation and impact

SilverPulse combines personalized physiological monitoring, data provenance, explainable analysis and simulated delayed medical communications in a single platform.

The goal is to support future development of tools that help astronauts and medical teams maintain accessible, structured health information during space missions.

Current limitations

SilverPulse is an experimental prototype. It uses synthetic astronaut scenarios, does not currently connect to real wearables, and has not undergone clinical validation.

The communication system is a simulation, not an implementation of NASA's operational DTN protocols. The spacecraft conversational assistant and a live generative AI service are not part of the verified demonstration.
